newsitem.title: USA: Stock prices mixed, await outcome of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stock prices mixed, await outcome of Fed meeting.

text.p: Stock prices were mixed Tuesday, with blue chips edging lower amid nervousness over the outcome of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting meeting and a sell-off in the shares of AT&T Corp.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was off 7.76 points at 5,886.98, retreating from Monday's record close of 5,894.74.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on moderate volume of 239 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 3.03 points at 1,214.50.

"This is about as wait-and-see kind of a day as you can find," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. adding that the market was dominated by short-term traders rather than portfolio managers.
The big question of the day was what action the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee would take on interest rates. The outcome was expected at 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).
In a Reuters survey of 55 primary dealers, banks and advisory firms, a slim majority of 31 forecasters said they expected the Fed to raise short-term interest rates.

"The message of the market today is that if the Fed does nothing or raises rates by 25 basis points (a quarter percentage point), the market will go up," Goldman said. "The only concern is a 50 basis point (half-point) increase and the chances of that are 10 to one against."
In the bond market, the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged at 7.02 percent.
AT&T dragged the Dow lower as the stock of the telecommunications giant lost 5-3/8 to 51-7/8 on a warnings that its earnings would disappoint.
"Were it not for AT&T, the Dow industrials would up 15 points," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
AT&T said higher sales and marketing costs, especially in its long distance business will pressure its third quarter results, and per share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates.
The sell-off in AT&T depressed other long-distance carriers. MCI Communications Corp. lost 1-1/8 to 26 and Sprint Corp. fell 1-1/2 to 40.

"We've all known that competition between the long-distance carriers, and between the carriers as a group and regional Bells and cable companies, will be intense over the next three to five years," said Johnson.
"People often ask themselves how this manifests itself, and here you have a very good example of how competitive the communications business has become," he said.
Among individual stocks, Micron Technology Inc. rose 2-3/8 to 30-3/8 after posting stronger-than-expected quarterly profits.
Microsoft Corp. was down 3/4 at 137 as investors became uneasy about a Justice Department probe into the company's Internet software business.
Texas Instruments Inc. was up 3-3/8 to 55-1/8 in sympathy with the rally in Micron.
